question: Your team uses Claude Code in a monorepo. The billing package has its own CLAUDE.md file with testing rules for that package. Two developers report that Claude Code follows these rules in some sessions and ignores them in others, even for similar tasks. Before anyone edits configuration files, you want to see which instruction files a session actually uses. What should you do first?

options.text: Split the billing CLAUDE.md file into topic-specific files in .claude/rules/, such as testing.md, so that the rules are easier for Claude Code to find.
options.reason: Splitting files into .claude/rules/ is a way to organize a large CLAUDE.md, not a way to verify which memory files a session has loaded.

options.text: Start each billing session in plan mode so that Claude Code explores the package and its configuration before it writes any code.
options.reason: Plan mode is for exploring and planning complex changes before execution; it does not show which memory files are loaded in a session.

options.text: Run the /memory command in a session that ignored the billing rules to see which memory files Claude Code has loaded.
options.reason: The guide names the /memory command as the way to verify which memory files are loaded and to diagnose inconsistent behavior across sessions.

options.text: Move the billing testing rules into the root CLAUDE.md file so that every session in the repository loads them.
options.reason: This changes the configuration before diagnosing the cause, and it removes the package scoping that the directory-level hierarchy provides.
